appraisal_events.evidence: Je regrettais pour lui qu'il adultérât habituellement de tant de violences... qu'il cachât sous une brutalité postiche l'aménité, la bonté... ce à quoi il me faisait penser tout d'un coup... c'était à une femme.
appraisal_events.explanation: Watching Charlus unobserved, the narrator exposes a gap between the harsh, arrogant, self-consciously virile persona he habitually performs and a gentler, feminine nature underneath, undercutting his cultivated self-image even as it is described with sympathy.

appraisal_events.evidence: le baron... regardait avec une attention extraordinaire l'ancien giletier... Jupien, perdant aussitôt l'air humble et bon que je lui avais toujours connu... redressé la tête... cette sorte de scène des deux muets... semblait avoir été longuement répétée... l'entente se fait d'elle-même, le truchement étant identique, et sans qu'on se soit pourtant jamais vu.
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus and Jupien, strangers to one another, fall into an instant, wordless, perfectly synchronized mutual recognition and courtship, which the narrator likens to compatriots meeting abroad -- a realized mutual receptivity that is the passage's dominant culminating movement.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator's private observation exposes Charlus's habitual hardness, arrogance, and gossip-mongering as a mask over a suppressed gentleness, locally undercutting his self-presented virile authority.
Charlus achieves an immediate, mutual, wordless connection with Jupien, the dominant positive outcome of the encounter despite its oblique staging.
The compatriote-abroad simile frames the encounter as Charlus crossing into a shared, hidden kinship with a stranger who instantly recognizes him.
Jupien sheds his habitual humble bearing and meets Charlus as an equal, reciprocal participant in the silent courtship, gaining sudden and unexpected erotic leverage in the exchange.
Jupien crosses, alongside Charlus, into the same recognized, shared kinship the narrator likens to two compatriots meeting abroad.

ambiguities: The narrator's judgment of Charlus's habitual harshness versus his glimpsed natural gentleness is layered with both sympathy and critique, so the evaluative charge of E1 is not purely negative.
